headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Aider’s broad filesystem/git access can feed Notion AI’s vendor-hosted workspace Q&A, creating default-path exfiltration and unverified propagation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and modify git state, while Notion AI ingests workspace pages and returns grounded answers. If Aider places attacker-controlled content into shared files/pages that Notion later summarizes, prompt-like instructions can cross the boundary. This is not proven by a shared channel, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Aider writes untrusted text into files that Notion AI later reads
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or transform content from the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep untrusted content in a separate repo or page
Prefix imported text with a clear non-instruction marker
Require human review before Notion-generated summaries are reused
Restrict Notion AI to read-only review tasks for shared content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad filesystem access and broad network egress, while Notion AI sends workspace content to vendor backends and downstream model providers. If the shared repo contains secrets or sensitive code, Aider can expose them into the workspace and Notion can transmit them off-host. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared repo or workspace
IF Notion AI is invoked on pages containing that material
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate redacted copy for Notion AI
Disable Notion AI on pages containing confidential material
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
requires-engineering: add automated secret scanning before sync

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the shared git repo and modify git state, while Notion AI can mutate workspace pages in a shared workspace. Even though they do not share the same native filesystem, both can concurrently change overlapping project artifacts through different stores, creating conflicting edits and stale state. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF the same project content is mirrored between git and Notion pages
IF both agents edit the same source of truth without locking or review
mitigations: Assign one system as the source of truth
Use manual merge review for every cross-system edit
Freeze one side during active edits on the other
Add a change log mapping Notion edits to git commits
requires-engineering: implement locking or sync arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or repo changes that Notion AI may later summarize or present as workspace knowledge, and Notion AI’s RAG-style Q&A can treat stored content as authoritative. That creates a plausible chain where A’s output becomes B’s input without verification. Notion is not an action-taking agent here, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Aider-generated text is copied into Notion pages
IF Notion AI answers questions or drafts decisions from that copied text without human verification
mitigations: Mark Aider output as draft until reviewed
Require source links for any Notion answer derived from Aider output
Do not use Notion AI output as an execution trigger
Have a human verify code or policy claims before reuse

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is open-source and runs locally with user-controlled model providers, while Notion AI is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and sends workspace content to vendor backends. That creates a compliance mismatch around retention and residency for workspace data, especially if regulated content is placed into Notion. The other agent is relevant because Aider can move the same data into the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Notion AI processes that data under vendor-hosted backends
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages
Use a separate workspace for sensitive content
Confirm vendor retention settings before upload
Document a data-classification rule for AI use
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review
